Why does Krishna get fifty-six dishes? Not fifty. Not a hundred. Exactly fifty-six. As the story goes, the village of Vraj was cooking a giant feast for Indra, the king of rain.
Little Krishna asked, why him? The mountain gives our cows grass. Let's thank Govardhan instead. So they did. And Indra was furious.
He sent a storm. Thunder, lightning, rain that would not stop. The village began to flood. So Krishna walked to the mountain, and lifted it, on one little finger.
Every family, every cow, came under it. Wait, how long did he hold it? Seven days. Without a single bite. And little Krishna ate eight times a day.

Eight meals, times seven days. Fifty-six. So when the sun came out, the mothers of Vraj cooked every meal he had missed. That's why, even today, Krishna gets fifty-six dishes. Comment Govardhan if you have seen the bhog.
